==Passive effect==
Against non-demonic enemies, Darklight is a fairly weak weapon with bonuses marginally better than that of a [[steel longsword]] with a lower strength bonus and a small, additional Magic Defence bonus. When used against [[Demon (attribute)|demonic]] monsters, however, Darklight provides a 60% increase in accuracy and damage.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1096470914395451392|date=15 February 2019|archiveurl=https://archive.is/zhVy3|archivedate=16 November 2020|quote=[Whats the damage increase against demons on the silver light exactly?] Treat your max hit as though it's 60% higher than it is.}} Some demons have modified demonbane effectiveness, which can either reduce or increase this bonus. For example, [[Duke Sucellus]] has 70% demonbane effectiveness, reducing the bonus to 42% accuracy and damage. Darklight also counts as a piece of [[silver weaponry]], and can therefore damage [[Vampyre (attribute)#Tier 2 Vampyres|tier 2 vampyres]], while gaining a 10% damage bonus against [[Vampyre (attribute)#Tier 1 Vampyres|tier 1 vampyres]].

The accuracy roll for ''Weaken'' is made against an opponent's stab defence,{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/793083437976543233|date=31 October 2016|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/vuwtr|archivedate=24 December 2022|quote=[Against what defensive style bonus does the special attack of the darklight/arclight roll against? The dds always uses slash.] Stab.}} and its drain effect only applies to [[successful hit]]s.

''Weaken'' will stack additively upon [[successful hit]]s unlike the [[dragon warhammer]], which stacks multiplicatively. Two successful special attacks thus reduce an opponent's Strength, Attack and Defence by 10% + 2, or 20% + 2 against demonic targets.

==Upgrading==
Darklight can be upgraded into [[Arclight]] by bringing three [[ancient shard]]s and using either the [[ancient shard]]s or Darklight on the [[Altar (Catacombs of Kourend)|Altar]] in the centre of the [[Catacombs of Kourend]]. Doing so further increases the effectiveness against [[Demon (attribute)|demonic]] monsters and changes the [[attack speed]] from 5 to 4 ticks. Attempting to use ancient shards on Darklight while not being at the altar results in the message {{mes|You require additional power from the catacombs altar to create Arclight.}}.

==Uses==
Bandos boots are often considered the "odd one out" of the Bandos armour set as they emphasise defensive bonuses, unlike the [[Bandos chestplate|chestplate]] and [[Bandos tassets|tassets]] which sacrifice melee defence (albeit a small amount) to give Strength bonus while the boots do not. This is the reason why most players, even while wearing Bandos armour, will usually opt for a different pair of boots in order to maximise their strength bonus. As a result, Bandos boots are significantly cheaper than the rest of the armour, despite being equally rare, due to their lack of demand.

However, their high ranged defence bonus makes them desirable for players trying to maximise their defensive bonuses. They are occasionally seen being used by [[ranged tank]]s due to their low cost and substantial defence bonus. Furthermore, they are effective when combined with the rest of the Bandos armour when trying to achieve an extremely high ranged defence bonus.

They are commonly used for protection against Bandos followers; wearing these boots will render followers of [[Bandos]] unaggressive to the wearer in the God Wars Dungeon. This makes them a good option for players hunting General Graardor, as they have the added benefit of prayer bonus and good tanking performance.

It should be noted that Bandos boots are, along with their successor [[guardian boots]], '''several''' times heavier than any other pair of boots in the game, with a weight of 6 kg. This makes them impractical for travel and dangerous skilling activities such as [[Pyramid Plunder]] or [[ZMI]].

==Passive effect==
When the accursed sceptre is charged with [[revenant ether]], an additional 50% magic accuracy and damage boost is applied when attacking any [[NPC]] in the [[Wilderness]], consuming 1 ether per attack whether the player hits or not. It is also applied to any [[combat spells]] cast when it is equipped, though it cannot [[autocast]] them in powered staff mode.

This effect will stack with a [[Slayer helmet (i)]] or a [[Salve amulet(i)]] and their variants, but not both simultaneously. This makes the sceptre the best magic weapon in the Wilderness, surpassing the damage output of a [[trident of the seas]] or [[Trident of the Swamp|swamp]] with the additional capability of attacking any hostile players, something which both tridents are incapable of doing.
Usage outside of the Wilderness will still consume 1 ether per attack, providing no passive effect. However, players can remove the ether and still autocast spells using an accursed sceptre (au).

However, if the target's levels are already deboosted by some amount, ''Condemn'' will only drain them up to 15%, but no further. As a result, multiple special attacks do not stack. For example, a target with level 80 Defence and Magic cannot have their stats drained lower than 68 if using Condemn.

Due to the [[powered staff]] version of this weapon having 1 [[Game tick|tick]] faster [[attack speed]], it may be preferable to use the "Swap" option to perform the [[Special attacks|special attack]], then swap back.

==Charging and death==
To use the sceptre's passive effect, it must first be activated with 1,000 [[revenant ether]] (costing {{NoCoins|{{GEP|Revenant ether|1000}}|c}}). The 1,000 ether used to activate the sceptre '''does not''' count towards the usage of the passive effect, thus additional ether must be added (up to 16,000) to increase the sceptre's damage output. Players can configure the charges while the sceptre is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. The hourly cost of constantly using this weapon to cast spells is 1,200 ether or {{NoCoins|{{GEP|Revenant ether|1200}}|c}}, as spells can only be cast every 5 [[game tick]]s.

cases.semanticExcerpt: '''Echo boots''' are an enhanced pair of [[guardian boots]] which require level 75 [[Defence]] to wear. They are made by combining the boots with an [[echo crystal]], a rare drop from participating in the [[Fortis Colosseum]]. secondaryExcerpts: Each echo crystal will add 6,000 charges to the recoil effect (costing {{Coins|{{GEP|Echo crystal}}/6000}} per charge), up to a maximum of 60,000. The recoil effect can be toggled via the boots' "Toggle-activity" option, allowing players to disable it as to not waste it during casual training, and instead use it in activities where the effect may prove more useful. The "Revert" option reverts the echo boots back into guardian boots, though this '''will not''' return any echo crystals, regardless of whether or not any recoil charges were used. Players can configure the charges while the boots are in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.
Like the Bandos and guardian boots used in their creation, they will render followers of [[Bandos]] [[unaggressive]] to the wearer in the [[God Wars Dungeon]].

This isn't my code, though, and I may simply be missing something.|ctxquote=@JagexAsh probably a question only you can answer lol - in pvp multi situations, does the confliction gauntlets passive effect only work on the player you're targeting or each player individually that's being affected by your ice barrage cast in the 3x3 clump}} This effect is disabled if using a [[Two-handed_slot_table|two-handed weapon]].

==Development history==
The passive effect of the confliction gauntlets was initially proposed without any restrictions.{{CiteNews|url=https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/new-delve-boss-rewards---varlamore-the-final-dawn?oldschool=1|title=New Delve Boss Rewards - Varlamore: The Final Dawn|newsdate=11 March 2025|quote=When you miss a Magic attack with the Gauntlets equipped, your next Magic attack of the same type (same weapon or spell), against the same enemy, will roll Accuracy twice. This means that if you're already hitting all of the time (looking at you, Shadow) you won't be benefiting much, but if your Accuracy is more middling you'll see some great returns.}} However, player concerns of making the [[Tumeken's shadow]] too powerful led to changes to prevent the gauntlets from interacting with it. The first change considered was for the passive to only apply for 4 ticks after a missed attack.{{CiteNews|url=https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/new-delve-boss-rewards---varlamore-the-final-dawn?oldschool=1|title=New Delve Boss Rewards - Varlamore: The Final Dawn|newsdate=24 March 2025|quote=When it comes to the Gauntlets, we hear your concerns regarding the Shadow. This reward, and project as a whole, doesn't have the scope to address specific Shadow issues, so what we have opted to do is make a tweak to the description of the passive. The Confliction Gauntlets' passive now reads: When a Magic attack misses, your next Magic attack within 4 ticks rolls accuracy twice. This means that you have 4 ticks to use the effect, with no down period between uses making you miss effects on other items. It's worth noting that this has to be against the same target and using the same spell or magic weapon. The same effect applies for a PvP target.}} Due to player concerns that this would cause the gauntlets to not benefit [[standard spellbook]] or [[Ancient Magicks]] spells, it was changed to its current effect instead, where the passive only functions with one-handed weapons. This restriction has been stated to potentially be removed in the future, if a theoretical rework of the Tumeken's shadow is released.{{CiteNews|url=https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/new-delve-boss-rewards---varlamore-the-final-dawn?oldschool=1|title=New Delve Boss Rewards - Varlamore: The Final Dawn|newsdate=28 March 2025|quote=That being said, our 'bandaid fix' for the Confliction Gauntlets was a tad divisive. In the short term, we're not going to be able to avoid a bandaid fix, but we do this in the knowledge that said bandaids can be pulled off whenever changes to Tumeken's Shadow are implemented. Some players pointed out that restricting the Gauntlets' effect to atacks within the next 4 ticks meant that Standard spells or Ancient Magicks wouldn't be able to benefit from them. This wasn't an oversight, we had some concerns around use-cases like freezes in PvP, blood spell healing in content where it's typically too inaccurate to be worth using, or potentially having to curtail Elemental Weaknesses to account for additional accuracy. We're not dead-set on any of these being overly problematic, so we'll be adjusting the Confliction Gauntlets' passive effect to remove the 4-tick restriction and instead benefit one-handed weapons only.}}
